items.title: From chat models to tool-using agents
items.summary: The important shift is no longer only model quality. Planning, tool selection, state, memory, and long-running execution are becoming part of the practical system design.
items.why_it_matters: Agent systems expose a new engineering layer between a language model and the real task environment. Reliability depends on orchestration, observable state, tool contracts, and failure handling.
items.research_connection: For robot task planning, this maps naturally to a high-level planner that selects perception and manipulation primitives instead of directly controlling low-level motion.

items.title: Why VLA systems matter for robot learning
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action models are a useful lens for tracking systems that connect visual context and language instructions to robot actions.
items.why_it_matters: They push robotics beyond isolated perception or planning modules and force us to think about how semantic understanding reaches the action space.
items.research_connection: This is directly relevant to separating VLM-based scene understanding from LLM-based high-level planning and later connecting both to manipulation skills.

items.title: What to watch in Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab
items.summary: Simulation quality matters less as a demo and more as a reproducible environment for policy learning, synthetic data, domain randomization, and robot evaluation.
items.why_it_matters: The practical question is whether the simulation stack supports the sensors, robot assets, training loop, and deployment path required by a real project.
items.research_connection: This is especially relevant when validating a robotics pipeline on available hardware before scaling experiments to newer GPUs or a different deployment machine.

items.title: VLMs are becoming an interface between perception and reasoning
items.summary: Instead of treating visual models only as detectors or segmenters, current multimodal systems can represent scene context in a form that downstream reasoning systems can use.
items.why_it_matters: That changes the role of perception from producing only coordinates or class labels to producing task-relevant semantic context.
items.research_connection: For manipulation tasks, this creates a design choice: what should remain deterministic perception and what should be delegated to a VLM.

items.title: A paper is worth tracking when it changes the design question
items.summary: The useful unit of reading is not every implementation detail. It is the problem, why the method was chosen, what assumption it changes, and what evidence supports the claim.
items.why_it_matters: This makes a daily research feed useful for deciding what deserves deeper reading instead of turning it into another unread backlog.
items.research_connection: The feed should surface papers that affect current work in LLM agents, VLMs, robot learning, manipulation, and simulation.
